result.title: Kernelized Parameter Sensitivity Atlases for Amortized Conditional Interpretability
result.summary: Gradient-based attribution provides input-specific information about model parameters, but computing it via backpropagation for many samples is expensive, while static importance scores discard input dependence. We derive KPSA (Kernelized Parameter Sensitivity Atlas) from a block decomposition of the empirical neural tangent kernel. It measures normalized parameter-group sensitivity, embeds those sources in an explicit query space, and uses a lightweight kernel to estimate sensitivities for unseen inputs. We derive bounds that separate finite-source from irreducible representation error and give margin-based top-$k$ recovery. This paper studies two interpretability applications. Firstly, KPSA identifies parameter groups with high susceptibility to perturbations across vision, forecasting, and protein-modeling setups. Across a fivefold range of parameter budgets ($0.02$-$0.1\%$), its selected groups attain $39$-$85\%$ of the perturbation susceptibility of a first-order backpropagation oracle. In vision and forecasting, these parameter groups form sparse sensitivity circuits that extend across depth and vary systematically with the input. Secondly, we use KPSA on an activation-attribution problem for MLP features in transformers. It retains $81\%$ of the gap between a backpropagation oracle and a constant-sensitivity baseline on vision while increasing batched query-time throughput from 551 to 2,041 images/s and reducing peak GPU memory from 4.55 to 0.44GB. On the protein-modeling task, it recovers $68\%$ of this gap. An ablation of KPSA's kernel aggregation shows that nearest-neighbor retrieval in KPSA space can remain competitive. The empirics show that compact kernel atlases can store useful input-dependent parameter sensitivity while amortizing repeated gradient attribution, a step toward scalable conditional interpretability. Code can be found at https://github.com/Axym-Labs/kpsa .

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 KPSA：从经验神经切核的分块分解导出参数组归一化敏感度，把敏感度来源嵌入显式查询空间，用轻量核为未见输入摊销估计敏感度，并在视觉、时序预测和蛋白质建模上评测参数组选择与 Transformer MLP 特征激活归因的保真度与吞吐/显存开销。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「摊销条件可解释性」可能为 LVR 提供廉价归因线索：以核图集替代逐样本反传来估计输入相关的参数与特征敏感度，可供核查能否用于定位 latent 推理中的视觉证据通路及贡献分配。
